title: Fasting insulin level predicted effector genes (Atla G et al. 2022)
bodyHtml:
This table displays predicted effector genes for fasting insulin levels, from the study:

Genetic regulation of RNA splicing in human pancreatic islets.
Atla G, et al.
Genome Biol . 2022 Sep 15;23(1):196. doi: 10.1186/s13059-022-02757-0.
PMID: 36109769

The authors mapped quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for mRNA levels (eQTLs) and splice junction usage (sQTLs) in 399 human pancreatic islets. To identify candidate effector genes, the authors performed a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using the FUSION algorithm (Gusev et al., 2016) with fasting insulin (adjusted for BMI) results from the Chen et al., 2021 study. For this purpose, expression and splicing junction usage weights were computed using RNA-seq and imputed genotypes generated in the study.

To complement TWAS results, the authors conducted colocalization analyses to test whether eQTLs and sQTLs were colocalized with GWAS associations for fasting insulin. Genes identified from TWAS analyses whose eQTLs or sQTLs colocalized with a fasting insulin GWAS signal with posterior probability ≥ 0.6, shown in the table below, represent candidate effector genes for fasting insulin levels.
